Subject: Post-demo recap — data handling & support access clarifications

Hi Julie / Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap from our side and three clarifying asks so we can produce the artifacts you requested: 

Key notes from the demo / discussion:
- Data residency: you said primary processing should remain in us-east-1 for FinPay production workloads.
- PII classes: two buckets discussed — transactional payment PII (higher retention needs) and ephemeral tokens/derivatives (shorter-term).
- Support access expectations: least-privilege support sessions, just-in-time elevation, and a documented break-glass approval workflow with an immutable audit trail.

Clarifying asks (can you confirm each?):
1) Retention windows: Is the requirement 7 years for transactional financial PII vs 90 days for ephemeral tokens? Please confirm exact retention per class.
2) Break-glass approvals: who at FinPay should be on the approver list (names/emails) and any SLA for approval (e.g., within 30 mins)?
3) Residency & subcontractors: confirm whether the processing location requirement applies to telemetry/logs as well as model inference, and whether FinPay allows subprocessor caching in a different region for ephemeral caching.

Next deliverables from Redwood once you confirm the above:
- Support access matrix (role -> privileges -> duration)
- Break-glass runbook (approval flow, audit fields, notification endpoints)
- SOC2 summary + evidence pointers we can share with your security team

Would love to lock a 30-minute follow-up Thu/Fri this week to walk through the proposed runbook and get signoff on approvers. I can also share the support matrix as a draft beforehand.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — data handling & support access clarifications

Connor —

Thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications from our side (we captured these on today's call but putting them in writing):

- Retention: for transactional PII tied to settlements we have a regulatory/business requirement to retain records up to 7 years. Ephemeral tokens and derived artifacts can be 90 days, but we need the ability to extend on a per-case basis for legal holds.
- Break-glass: approvers will be me (Julie Harris) and our Head of Ops (Alex Rivera). We need approvals logged and timestamps immutable; 30-minute SLA is fine but not strictly required — we need an audit trail and notification to our security mailbox.
- Logs & telemetry: audit logs and request traces must remain in us-east-1 and be retained for 3 years; we will not allow permanent offshoring of audit logs. Short-lived caching for latency (under 15 minutes) in a nearby region is tolerable if the cache never persists PII and is evictable.

We will send over an internal redline of the data-classification mapping (attached: FinPay-data-classification-v2.xlsx) so you can map your matrix to ours.

Can you provide the SOC2 control evidence pointers and a draft of the break-glass runbook by EOD Weds? That will give our security team time to review before a follow-up call.

Appreciate it — Julie

Hi Julie / Alex —

Following up with the deliverables we discussed. Attached are two artifacts: support-access-matrix.xlsx and soc2-evidence-summary.pdf. High-level summary below and notes on how we meet your asks.

Summary of proposed controls:
- Roles & least privilege: we propose three scoped support roles (Observer, Scoped-Responder, Escalation-Engineer). Each role has explicit allowed operations and target namespaces.
- Just-in-time elevation: elevated sessions issued via the customer SSO / OIDC flow for a time-bound session (default 1 hour), with an option for manual extension and mandatory approver (FinPay approver list).
- Break-glass flow: emergency elevation triggers a push notification to approvers (SMS+email) and creates an immutable ticket in our audit log. All break-glass events require post-facto justification and are flagged to your security mailbox.
- Audit & retention: every support session record includes request_id, user_id, approver_id, start/end timestamps, action list, and a full exportable audit bundle. Audit logs are stored in us-east-1 and retained 3 years by default (configurable).
- Telemetry caching: we support ephemeral caching in a sister region for up to 15 minutes; caching of PII is explicitly disabled and enforced via a data-classification filter.

Attached notes: mapping from FinPay classes (your spreadsheet) to Redwood's retention tiers, and a pointer to the controls in the SOC2 summary PDF.

Next steps / timeline:
- Wed EOD (2026-05-13): Connor to organize 30-min signoff call and upload artifacts to HubSpot deal FP-4832 (I attached the files here as well).
- Thu (2026-05-14): Security review — we will standby for your redlines and can iterate.
